method: C_H(P,L) = Cov_i(sigma_H(frame_i), O_i) over twirl instances i at fixed (target P, depth L). label = NET twirl-frame byproduct Pauli. Our theorem's coherent signature is GROWTH of |C| with depth (per-cycle accumulation).

our_signature_test.definition: weighted slope of |C(L)| vs L; positive => coherent accumulation with depth (per-cycle labels). Assessed against a frame-permutation null over all 135 (H,target) tests.
our_signature_test.conclusion: NO depth-growing coherent accumulation above the null.

shallow_correlation.definition: |C| at the shallowest depth (L=2), max over 135 tests, vs frame-permutation null.
shallow_correlation.interpretation: A small (|C|~0.02) but statistically real label-outcome correlation exists at shallow depth; it DECAYS toward zero with depth (does not accumulate). Physically: the net frame is the PRODUCT of the per-cycle Paulis, so it decorrelates from any single cycle's coherent contribution as depth grows. Caveat: at shallow depth this correlation cannot be cleanly separated from readout-asymmetry (which also makes the sign-corrected survival frame-dependent) without per-layer labels.

positive_control.interpretation: Injecting a label-correlated shift theta_inj recovers C ~= theta_inj with the expected error -> the estimator is correct. A null on real data is therefore a property of the DATA/label, not a code bug.

noise_floor.note: With C=60 randomizations the per-depth covariance floor is ~0.0052 (1 sigma). Resolving a depth-ACCUMULATING coherent covariance would require logging PER-LAYER twirl labels (not present here) and/or many more randomizations.

verdict: This real-hardware CB dataset exposes only the NET twirl frame. Our estimator (validated by the positive control and by the §2 fidelity match) finds a genuine but shallow, NON-accumulating label-outcome correlation and NO depth-growing coherent signal. This is the STRUCTURAL outcome anticipated in the spec: the per-cycle coherent information our theorem shows is recoverable requires per-layer labels, motivating a purpose-built RC experiment that logs them.
